research_question: In people with first-episode or recent-onset psychosis, what is the effect of adding cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to standard care compared to standard care alone or an active control on negative symptoms?
control_label: Standard care alone or active psychosocial control plus standard care
outcome_description: Severity of negative symptoms of psychosis measured by validated psychiatric rating scales (such as PANSS negative subscale, SANS, BNSS, or CAINS), selecting one endpoint per study with preference for medium-term follow-up (<= 12 months).
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater reduction/improvement in negative symptoms (fewer negative symptoms) in the CBT group compared to the control group.
search_queries: first episode psychosis cognitive behavioral therapy negative symptoms trial
recent onset psychosis CBT PANSS negative symptoms randomized controlled
early psychosis cognitive behaviour therapy negative symptoms effect outcome
inclusion_criteria: Participants diagnosed with first-episode psychosis (FEP) or recent-onset psychosis/schizophrenia spectrum disorders.
Evaluation of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT or CBT for psychosis) added to standard care versus standard care alone or an active control intervention.
Quantitative measurement of negative symptoms of psychosis using a validated assessment scale (e.g., PANSS negative subscale, SANS, BNSS, CAINS).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, study protocols, and theoretical papers are excluded).
No comparison between a CBT treatment condition and a control condition (standard care alone or active control).
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size for negative symptoms (e.g., means, standard deviations, change scores, t/F values, or test statistics).
Completely unrelated to first-episode or recent-onset psychosis or does not measure negative symptoms.
moderators_to_extract: Control condition type (treatment-as-usual vs. active psychosocial control)
Measurement instrument (e.g., PANSS negative subscale vs. SANS vs. other validated scales)
Intervention format (individual vs. group vs. blended/digital CBT)
Assessment timing (post-intervention vs. medium-term follow-up within 12 months)
Intervention dosage / planned number of CBT sessions
effect_size_note: Standardized mean differences (Hedges' g) aligned such that positive effect sizes represent greater reduction in negative symptoms (favoring CBT). One endpoint is selected per study, prioritizing medium-term follow-up (<= 12 months).
